newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah weakens in late trading.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah weakens in late trading.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah weakened against the dollar in moderate late trading on Tuesday.
Dealers said ample rupiah supply and unconfirmed television reports of a bomb threat in a north Jakarta shopping mall seemed to unsettle the market and caused the rupiah to weaken.
The private Surya Citra Televisi Indonesia reported on there was a bomb threat in a north Jakarta shopping centre and three suspects had been detained.
However, the police could not confirm the action.
One district police official denied the incident.
Dealers said they were surprised with the reaction to the news as it was reported early in the morning and the market was not affected for quite a while.
"The market was pretty quiet this morning and people seemed to have shrugged off the news. I don't know why people were linking the afternoon fall to the television report," one said.
But some dealers attributed the decline to excess rupiah supply in the afternoon, with overnight money falling to two percent from 7.0/9.0 percent at the opening.
Overnight swaps declined to -0.05/0.05 points.
Tom/next was at 0.05/0.15 points.
"I think it's also partly due to the ample rupiah supply," one local bank dealer said, adding that operators remained cautious in the run-up to Thursday's general elections.
Spot rupiah, due Friday because the central bank will have no clearing on Thursday, declined to 2,441.0 before settling at 2,440.40/41.40 at 0900 GMT from an opening of 2,437.5/38.5.
Tomorrow and today rupiah ended at 2,440.40/40.90 and 2,438.5/39.0, respectively.
Dealers said the underlying tone for the dollar turned biddish in the afternoon after sliding on profit-taking.
But they said swap rates tended to soften on cheap short-term funds. "Short-term rates are too low to go long further in forwards," one foreign bank dealer said.

One dealer in Singapore said earlier offshore operators were also seen overborrowing the rupiah in the forward market fearing a possible rupiah squeeze by Bank Indonesia if it were to copy Thai steps to curb speculation.
However, the central bank said there was no such plan.
One-month swaps eased to 13.25/13.75 from 14.0/15.5, two to 26.0/28.5 from 27.0/29.0, three to 38.0/40.0 from 40.0/42.0 and six to 76.0/76.5 from 76.0/79.0 points.
The central bank raised its intervention band by one point to 2,414/2,606 but lowered its conversion band by one point to 2,415/2,463 on Tuesday.
